commit.message:
Match MuJoCo's incident-face selection for plane-mesh contacts (#1731)

* Pick the plane-convex contact points among all penetrating vertices

plane_convex takes the deepest vertex and picks up to three more among the vertices within 1 mm of its depth. A face tilted into the plane by more than 1 mm across its width therefore gets every contact on its deepest edge: a 10 cm plate tilted 3 degrees, its bottom face 1 to 6 mm into the plane, gets 2 contacts on one edge where MuJoCo gets the face's 4 corners. A body landing on such a face is then held up at one edge alone and sinks.

This picks the other points among all penetrating vertices, in the exhaustive and the graph search alike. A body less than 1 mm into the plane, as at rest, keeps its contacts: the graph search's threshold was already clamped at 0 there.

The new mesh_plane_tilted_plate (8 vertices, the exhaustive search) and mesh_plane_tilted_plate_graph (12 vertices, the graph search) fixtures fail without the change (MuJoCo's contact 1 is not found) and pass with it.

* Test a plane-mesh face pressed under a rim above the plane

The mesh_plane_rim_above_plane fixture from #1728: a plate 0.2 mm into the plane with a wider rim 0.3 mm above it, which MuJoCo touches at the plate's 4 corners. It fails at main, where the exhaustive search's threshold is unclamped and picks rim vertices above the plane, which write_contact drops (1 contact), and passes with the threshold at 0.

* Match MuJoCo's incident-face selection for plane-mesh contacts

Choose the polygon incident to the deepest support vertex whose normal most opposes the plane, then reduce it with MuJoCo's anchored hull4f algorithm. Evaluate support in mesh-local coordinates and initialize the graph climb from the support of its starting vertex. Keep the mesh-center filter and leave margin and gap filtering to write_contact.

Require matching contact counts and ordered geometry against MuJoCo C, enable the complex mesh fixture with an unambiguous face orientation, and cover polygon pruning with nonzero mesh offsets, exhaustive search, separated contacts, a distant plane origin, and the mesh-center filter. The previous implementation fails all nine selection cases; removing the mesh-center filter fails its dedicated regression.

* Return early from plane_convex for a mesh separated past margin plus gap

plane_convex takes the pair's margin plus gap and returns after the deepest vertex's contact when that vertex lies farther from the plane, as mjc_PlaneConvex returns past its margin, so a mesh admitted by the bounding-sphere filter no longer runs the incident-polygon lookup, the hull4 reduction and the secondary vertex transforms for contacts that write_contact drops. max_support starts at -MJ_MAXVAL in place of the 1e6 constant left over from the removed spread heuristic. The plane-mesh selection assertions discard the contacts put_data copies from MuJoCo before mjw.collision runs, so they read Warp's own output.
